body.en: In uniform circular motion the speed is constant but the direction of the velocity keeps changing, so there is an acceleration. It points towards the centre and has magnitude $a_c = v^2/R$. This is the *centripetal* (centre-seeking) acceleration. Its direction keeps changing, so it is not a constant vector.
body.kn: ಏಕರೂಪ ವರ್ತುಲ ಚಲನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಜವ ಸ್ಥಿರ, ಆದರೆ ವೇಗದ ದಿಕ್ಕು ಸದಾ ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಕೇಂದ್ರದ ಕಡೆಗೆ v²/R ಪರಿಮಾಣದ ಕೇಂದ್ರಾಭಿಮುಖ ವೇಗೋತ್ಕರ್ಷ ಇರುತ್ತದೆ. ಅದರ ದಿಕ್ಕು ಬದಲಾಗುವುದರಿಂದ ಅದು ಸ್ಥಿರ ಸದಿಶವಲ್ಲ.

title.en: Whirl a stone, then cut the string

narration.en: In uniform circular motion the speed v = ωr stays the same but the direction keeps changing, so there is an acceleration v²/r = ω²r towards the centre, given by the tension. Cut the string and the centripetal force vanishes: the stone flies off along the tangent, not outwards.
narration.kn: ಏಕರೂಪ ವೃತ್ತೀಯ ಚಲನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ವೇಗ v = ωr ಒಂದೇ, ಆದರೆ ದಿಕ್ಕು ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತಲೇ ಇರುತ್ತದೆ; ಹಾಗಾಗಿ ಕೇಂದ್ರದ ಕಡೆಗೆ v²/r = ω²r ವೇಗೋತ್ಕರ್ಷ, ಅದನ್ನು ದಾರದ ಸೆಳೆತ ಕೊಡುತ್ತದೆ. ದಾರ ಕತ್ತರಿಸಿದರೆ ಕೇಂದ್ರಾಭಿಮುಖ ಬಲ ಇಲ್ಲ: ಕಲ್ಲು ಸ್ಪರ್ಶಕದ ದಿಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಹಾರುತ್ತದೆ, ಹೊರಗಲ್ಲ.

body.en: *Angular speed* $\omega = \Delta\theta/\Delta t$ is measured in rad/s, and the linear speed is $v = \omega R$. The period T is the time for one revolution and the frequency is ν = 1/T, so $\omega = 2\pi\nu = 2\pi/T$ and $a_c = 4\pi^2\nu^2 R$.
body.kn: ಕೋನೀಯ ಜವ ω = Δθ/Δt (rad/s). ರೇಖೀಯ ಜವ v = ωR. ಆವರ್ತನಾವಧಿ T ಮತ್ತು ಆವರ್ತನ ν = 1/T; ω = 2πν = 2π/T.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. An insect trapped in a circular groove of radius 12 cm moves steadily and completes 7 revolutions in 100 s. Find its angular speed, linear speed and acceleration.

say.en: Let us solve this together. An insect trapped in a circular groove of radius 12 centimetres moves steadily and completes 7 revolutions in 100 seconds. Find its angular speed, linear speed and acceleration.
nu equals 7 over 100 equals 0.07 rev/s, so omega equals 2 pi nu is approximately 0.44 rad/s.
v equals omega R equals 0.44 times 12 is approximately 5.3 centimetres per second.
a equals omega squaredR equals 0.44 squared times 12 is approximately 2.3 centimetres per second squared, directed towards the centre.
So the answer is omega is approximately 0.44 rad/s, v is approximately 5.3 centimetres per second, a is approximately 2.3 centimetres per second squared towards the centre.

problem.en: A stone tied to a 0.5 m string is whirled in a horizontal circle at 2 revolutions per second. Find its centripetal acceleration.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A stone tied to a 0.5 m string is whirled in a horizontal circle at 2 revolutions per second. Find its centripetal acceleration.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A stone tied to a 0.5 metres string is whirled in a horizontal circle at 2 revolutions per second. Find its centripetal acceleration.
omega equals 2 pi times 2 equals 4 pi rad/s.
a equals omega squaredR equals 16 pi squared times 0.5 equals 8 pi squared is approximately 79 metres per second squared.
So the answer is About 79 metres per second squared.
